We are citizens, and residents of London, and our names are Thomas and Richard Jones, and we carry on business together, as chemists and druggists, in the street which was formerly named Long, but which has recently been changed to Broad street, where we have lived ten years, and have acquired a considerable portion of our neighbours' good will, in consequence of punctuality in our engagements, and a desire to be neat and orderly in our personal habits. Thomas was born in the west, and Richard in the east, of the city, and, for a long time, we had no more than sufficient to maintain two good friends, but, by degrees, we have become prosperous enough to be able to live comfortably, and to assist each other in time of need.
